extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, MathOverflow users, and readers interested in online math-community moderation
extracted.subtask_description: Judging whether questions and commentary are appropriate for MathOverflow and how moderation/community norms should be applied; includes views on focus, rigor, historical/motivational content, and handling of commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is this question a good fit for MO?
rubrics_metrics.description: The recurring community/ moderator question: 'Is this question a good fit for MO?'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author criticizes excessive, hair-splitting debate about 'fit' (described as a 'perverse puritanical hair-splitting competition') and argues that such gatekeeping can exclude worthwhile questions; community acceptance (e.g., upvotes and answers) should weigh in. The phrase is presented as the main, sometimes over-invoked, criterion for closure/migration decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus / 'not focused enough' as closure reason
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions may be closed or deemed inappropriate if they are 'not focused enough'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The post reports that some askers had their questions closed for lack of focus and objects to excessive strictness. Implicit guidance: consider whether less-focused but collegial or historically/motivationally interesting questions deserve a place rather than automatic closure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research-level / 'research' vs 'pure' mathematics suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a question meets the site's implied standard of research-level mathematics or the community's evolving notion of 'research' mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author notes a shift in how 'research' mathematics is conceived on MO and implies that strict adherence to a narrow conception can be exclusionary; questions with historical or motivational flavor may still be valuable even if not strictly technical research problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigor vs collegial opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: The tension between requiring perfectly rigorous, technical answers and allowing 'free, collegial opinion, even if not perfectly rigorous'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The post's commenters express a desire for the site to allow collegial, less formal commentary; the author favors preserving discussion and motivation rather than enforcing only rigorous, formal responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community signals (upvotes/answers) as indicators of acceptability
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of upvotes and presence of decent answers indicate that 'to most readers, the question and the answer are perfectly fine.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use community reactions (votes, answers) as evidence of a question's value; strong positive community response can counter isolated critical commentary about fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation strictness and etiquette policing
rubrics_metrics.description: Critique of moderators/participants who spend excessive effort policing etiquette and question appropriateness, sometimes at the expense of substantive mathematical contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author warns that vocal critics who focus on etiquette can be detrimental, and suggests moderation should avoid overzealous hair-splitting and consider the broader mathematical value of contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve history, motivation and insights
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions or answers that provide history, motivation and insights into mathematics are valuable and should not be discarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author asks rhetorically what historical/motivational figures would think if modern practice threw away history and motivation; implicit guidance: allow and value contextual, motivational, and historical discussion, not only narrow technical Q&A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling extended commentary (move vs keep)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether extended negative commentary should remain attached to a question or be moved off-site/archived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The post notes an example where commentary was moved off-site and the question kept with an unobtrusive pointer to the discussion; this is presented as a reasonable way to preserve the Q&A while removing distracting debate.
